Complete biased rant but whatever. This is eomthing i noticed after a while of using the QT framework, and why it will never really take off beyond the open source dev tool.

The first thing is the prohibitive licensing model which makes any commercial use of the QT framework horribly expensive. I think the price went down over the years, but it was still a pretty penny for a license between 5 years ago and now. This is a really hard sell when you have JavaFX, and WPF which are both being offered for free and have commercial support. And on one hand i understand the company has to make money, but i feel a UDK model would have made more sense for the target audience who would use this product.

Language wise, this framework is aggravating. It uses macros for everything, and the resource ownership means you cant use any of the new c++ goodies. You HAVE to use the QT way of doing things. Speaking of macros, it looks like QT loves macros. I can understand why, but i would think in the later installments they could have created a hybrid QObject inheritance for qml elements so that any derived q object classes could be automatically made into qml elements. Instead another macro was created to get rid of qmlRegisterType.

The last thing is that QML is nice, but holy shit does it have so many quirks. The inheritance model is all over the place, the intellisense sucks beyond all hell, and the architecture makes for a very steep learning curve once you go beyond a basic example. I usually use the qml files only with adding my own changes, but you can definitely tell QT wants you to use the designer for this. The problem is i hate designers because of how constrictive they are. So now you end up with either a choice of a qml file, or a qml ui file which has two files, the boilerplate and the ui file itself. The worst part is qml files can be opened in designer without a ui file, which makes me wonder why the fuck there has to be two versions of what amounts to the same thing?
